summary: Iteration 6 - Verified v2 features: student kiosk attendance (attend-student + sync), student PATCH (edit modal + API), and admin stats students_present. All 10 new backend tests pass. Full pytest suite is 62/62 green when run serially (-n0). Under parallel default (`-n 2 --dist loadscope`) 4 tests fail due to state-races between settings-mutating tests and kiosk attend tests — this is a known limitation of --dist loadscope which does NOT honor xdist_group markers (loadgroup does). Frontend student kiosk flow works end-to-end; admin edit-student modal works and persists via PATCH. DB state preserved (teachers=2, students=120, attendance=1).

minor.issue: pytest.ini uses `--dist loadscope`, which ignores `xdist_group` markers. Cross-module state races (settings mutation vs. kiosk attend) surface as 4 flake failures. Serial run (-n0) is 62/62 green. Consider switching to `--dist loadgroup` to actually honor the xdist_group serialization.

action_items: (Optional, low-priority) Switch pytest.ini from `--dist loadscope` to `--dist loadgroup` so the existing `xdist_group(name='demo_school_settings')` markers actually serialize the stateful demo-school tests across parallel workers. The 4 failing cases under the default parallel config all pass serially and represent race conditions, not real bugs.

(Optional) Cleanup: `TestStudentPatch.test_patch_and_restore` in new test file uses NIS 10120 (last demo student). Could collide if another stateful test on the same school ever touches 10120. Currently unique.

rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bug found. The only 'failure' under parallel default config is a pytest orchestration issue: --dist loadscope does not honor pytest.mark.xdist_group; only --dist loadgroup does. Because the demo-school-settings tests mutate shared server state (work_start, invoice generation, attendance records), running them on different xdist workers races. Mitigation: run with -n0 for a clean signal (documented in pytest.ini comment already), or switch dist to loadgroup.
